record.original_question: If a manifold carries an SU(2)-action and its orbit space satisfies a suitable geometric condition, such as carrying an Einstein metric, must the manifold itself admit an Einstein metric?

evidence.quote: Question 3.10. Does a manifold with a \(\mathrm{SU}(2)\)-action always admit an Einstein metric if the orbit space satisfies some nice condition such as the existence of an Einstein metric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a smooth (effective) action of the Lie group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and let $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ denote the corresponding orbit space. A Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$.

Determine whether the following implication holds: if the orbit space $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ carries a "nice" geometric structure—in particular, if it admits an Einstein metric (in the appropriate orbifold/stratified sense)—then $M$ itself must admit an Einstein metric. Equivalently, formulate and prove (or disprove by counterexample) general conditions on the orbit space $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ under which an Einstein metric on $M/\mathrm{SU}(2)$ guarantees the existence of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-invariant Einstein metric on $M$.
artifact.category_tag: Einstein metrics with Lie group actions
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of when an SU(2)-action on a manifold with a "nice" orbit space (e.g., one admitting an Einstein metric) guarantees an invariant Einstein metric on the total space remains open. Partial results exist in special settings: cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics constructed by Böhm in dimensions 5–9, recent computer-assisted constructions of SU(2)-invariant negative Einstein metrics, and Kähler–Einstein metrics with SU(2)-action in dimension four. No general theorem matching the broad formulation is known.

status_evidence.title: Computer-assisted construction of SU(2)-invariant negative Einstein metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work constructs SU(2)-invariant negative Einstein metrics, identifying 2-parameter families for each of four singular orbit topologies.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of SU(2)-invariant Einstein metrics is studied case-by-case, indicating no general orbit-space criterion is known.

status_evidence.title: Kähler–Einstein metrics with SU(2) action
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes Kähler–Einstein metrics in real dimension four admitting an isometric SU(2) action with generically three-dimensional orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Only special-case existence results are available.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Einstein Metrics on 4-Manifolds (Anderson)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of existence and obstructions for Einstein metrics; no general theorem deriving Einstein metrics from properties of the orbit space.
status_evidence.claim: The general question stated remains unresolved in the literature.
